Apple previously said it could no longer absorb sharply rising memory costs, and has since raised prices on most products significantly. iPhone pricing is expected to rise again when new models launch this September.

Most people were already pessimistic, believing these increases would be permanent, despite Apple's claims it was working hard to address the problem. Now the situation looks set to worsen, as TSMC is raising chip fabrication prices…

Apple price hikes

Apple last month announced price increases of over 50% in some cases — with memory and storage upgrades doubling in price in some instances. At the time, it said it was pulling out all the stops to tackle the problem.

9to5Mac readers mostly did not believe this, and expected the high pricing to remain in place. Almost all said it would change their buying behaviour, mainly by upgrading their devices less frequently.

TSMC raises chip fabrication prices

Now things look set to get worse. Nikkei Asia reports that TSMC, Apple's chip foundry, plans to raise its chip manufacturing service prices from next year.

The report says the Taiwanese company has completed negotiations with customers, with increases of between 5% and 10%. When customer orders exceed original forecasts, the chipmaker may also charge an additional premium of up to 15%. If Apple underestimates demand for new products, this could be affected.

TSMC declined to comment, saying only that it continues to work closely with customers to reflect the value of its services.

TSMC has previously said it may eventually build a total of twelve chip fabrication plants in Arizona, but this remains viewed with scepticism.
